sources.supports: Android phone & tablet deletion help: touch and hold each message then 'At the top, tap Delete'; 'Delete multiple messages quickly': touch and hold, 'At the top left, tap the box next to "Select all."', by default 'Gmail selects up to 50 messages to delete', to select 50 more scroll to the top and tap the Select all box again, then tap Delete; enter a search operator (From:, after:/before:, has:attachment) to delete specific emails; Empty trash: Menu > Trash > 'Empty trash now'; restore: Menu > Trash > touch and hold > More (top right) > Move to; swipe: Menu > Settings > General settings > Swipe actions, next to Right/Left swipe tap Change, choose Delete; Trash recovery up to 30 days then permanent; deleted drafts can't be recovered from Trash.

A reviewer should open the page directly to confirm exact labels.

serp_review.observation: Results: blog.incogni.com (phone deletion guide, two URLs), nira.com (two URLs), clean.email (competitor; Android 'delete all at once' guide), techloy.com, geeksforgeeks.org, theexchange.africa web story, plus low-quality aggregator pages. Snippets conflicted: one says tap the sender avatar to select, one says long-press reveals Select all, one says the app has no built-in Select All and recommends Chrome Desktop View, one says mobile is limited to 50-message batches and large deletions need a desktop browser.
serp_review.limitation: One standard US web search; result pages weren't opened, so the characterisation rests on titles and snippets only. Desktop View in mobile Chrome is a separate pending topic (gmail-select-all-conversations-desktop-site-mobile) and the draft makes no claim about it.

information_gain: A source-checked, Gmail-Android-app-specific procedure (search first, Select all box, 50-message default, repeat-then-delete) with a rounds table, a 'delete all' decision table that absorbs the deferred delete-all-emails-gmail-app-android intent (sender / promotions / date / whole inbox, what to watch, and the note that clearing Inbox leaves archived mail), a reconciliation of the conflicting SERP advice (avatar tap, 'no Select all', other mail apps), and the Android-specific swipe path (General settings > Swipe actions > Change > Delete) and restore path (More > Move to). Published pages only carry a one-paragraph Android aside each; none is device-dedicated.
